HIFZEF.note: Pt(II) with neutral phosphines, not Pt(IV) with anionic phospholides (same total charge 0, but the anionic-P + Pt(IV) d-count wreck the xtb relaxation).

ROQDOQ.note: [Co(NCS)4]2- is Co(II) d7 (uhf 3), not Co(IV) d5 (uhf 1). The wrong d5 low-spin doublet let xtb relax the tetrahedron flat to square planar (pre-opt poly 0.2 -> 31); Co(II) d7 keeps it tetrahedral.

AMUJUO.note: CSD extraction built the wrong ligands: an anionic beta-diketiminate + a benzene TRIANION instead of the real NEUTRAL bis-aryl alpha-diimine (N,N chelate) + NEUTRAL 1,3,5-triphenylbenzene (eta6 arene). User-supplied SMILES. Both ligands neutral -> V(0), total charge 0 (was V(IV) balancing -4). OS is the neutral-complex reading; verify against the crystal counterion count.

INIHOD.note: Same broken ligand as AMUJUO: the third ligand is the NEUTRAL bis-aryl alpha-diimine (user-supplied SMILES), not the anionic beta-diketiminate. With Cl- + amide- + neutral diimine the total ligand charge is -2 -> V(II), total charge 0 (was V(III) balancing -3). Verify OS against the crystal.

UMIZOG.note: The mesityl carbanion binds through its DEPROTONATED ring carbon ([c-], atom 2), not a neighbouring CH (atom 5). Donor-only fix.

MUTSAX.note: User-corrected ligand SMILES: the SAME molecule as the mined one (identical canonical skeleton) but re-drawn and with the [c-] carbanion neutralised. Binds through the same 2 P + 2 central-ring C = new atoms 2,8,36,47 (were 3,10,11,19). The neutral tetradentate is on Ni(0) (d10), so the complex is neutral (total charge 0); ligand charge -1 -> 0 and OS 1 -> 0 together keep it neutral.
